column2: A new face has come asking to join [Root.Society.GetName]: [new_recruit.GetTitledName]. Our ways are old and plain. No one sits among us who has not first fought before us. I should go and tell the [new_recruit.GetManWoman] what is expected.
The Gods want blood. Let us see whose.
Yes-yes, new claw-fodder. Let it fight-prove!
Time ta see if dis one's got any fight in 'im.
I'll put on my sternest face. The Wolf likes that.
I shall explain the customs of the order.
Another beardling. Let's see what their steel is worth.
I'll put on my most fearsome face. Ahem.
You will meet §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! and explain the trial by combat.

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] looks at me through the slits of a helm crusted with old blood. "You want to walk the road to glory, [Root.GetBoyGirl]? Then you will walk it over someone. The Gods do not want words. They want to see you fight." An armoured fist points at the ring of warriors behind. "One of mine. Now. Win, or bleed well enough that the Gods take notice."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] circles me, sniffing, tail lashing. "You want-wish to serve the Warlords? Hmm-hmm. Many want. Few live. You fight one of my clawpack, yes-yes? Fight-win and you are of [champion_character.Society.GetName]. Fight-lose and..." The Skaven chitters. "Then we feast tonight."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] yellz right in me face. "Oi! Ya wanna join da boyz? Den ya gotta pruv ya ain't a runt, [Root.GetBoyGirl]." Da big git folds 'is armz an' grins wiv all 'is teef. "Ya fight one of da ladz. Ya win, ya'z in. Ya lose... well, it'll be funny anyway."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] meets me in the cold of the yard, a wolfskin over [champion_character.GetHerHis] shoulders. "Ulric gives nothing to those who ask, [Root.GetBoyGirl]. He gives to those who take." [champion_character.GetSheHe] nods at the warriors around the fire. "You will fight one of ours. Stand, and the Wolf will know your name. Fall and get up again, and he still might."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] receives me in the order's hall, beneath the banners of old campaigns. "Courage is not proven by asking, [Root.GetLordLady]. Our custom is a passage of arms with a brother or sister of the order, before witnesses." [champion_character.GetSheHe] gestures to the lists outside. "Acquit yourself with honour and you will be welcome. Shame yourself, and no gate of ours will open to you again."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] strokes [champion_character.GetHerHis] beard and looks me up and down for a long while. "Words are cheap, [Root.GetFirstName]. Steel is not. The Guild does not take a warrior for a good name or a long beard. You will fight one of ours, and the elders will watch. And mind, if you run, it goes in the book."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] greets me with a curt nod. "Another recruit? To sit among us you must prove yourself, [Root.GetBoyGirl]," the [champion_character.GetManWoman] says gruffly, arms folded. "You will fight one of our own. Win, or at least do not disgrace yourself, and you are welcome."

[champion_character.GetTitledName] of [champion_character.Society.GetName] eyes me up and down, doubtful at first, and then [champion_character.GetHerHis] face changes. "Hold. Are you of the blood of [founder_target.GetTitledFirstName]?" I nod. "Then the old songs walk in here with you! The trial is the same for everyone, mind. But I will be watching you very closely."
Let the Gods watch, then.
Yes-yes! I fight-win, quick-quick!
I'll smash 'im up!
Then I will fight, and the Wolf may judge me.
I accept the passage of arms.
Bring them on. My axe is sharp.
I will gladly fight to prove myself.
You agree to duel whoever §Y[champion_character.Society.GetNameCap]§! chooses for you.
On second thought, I prefer my blood inside me.
Wait-wait! I am... busy. Important-busy.
Skah, ain't joinin' sum dum mob!
Perhaps the hearth is warmer than the yard.
I fear I must withdraw my request.
Another year, perhaps. When my beard is longer.
Actually, I would rather not bloody my knuckles.
You will not try to join §Y[champion_character.Society.GetNameCap]§!.

[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName] did not flinch when I explained our custom. The [new_recruit.GetManWoman]'s eyes lit up at the thought of a fight. After asking around, [duel_target.GetTitledName] has offered to cross weapons with the newcomer.
[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName] listened to me explain our custom, then shook [new_recruit.GetHerHis] head and walked off. "Bleed for a seat at your table? I think not."
Show [new_recruit.GetHerHim] how it's done, [duel_target.GetFirstName].
A sparring duel will take place between §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledName]§! and §Y[duel_target.GetTitledName]§!.
Why, that little... The coward!
None of us expected much, but [From.GetBestName] came through the initiation duel without a scratch. It will be worth watching what the [From.GetManWoman] makes of [From.GetHerselfHimself] among us.

[From.GetBestName] took some bruises and a cut or two, but held [From.GetHerHis] ground well. I was not the only one who was pleased. Time will tell whether our road suits the [From.GetAgeAdjective] [From.GetManWoman].

[From.GetBestName] was badly hurt by [combatant_2.GetTitledFirstName], and still got back on [From.GetHerHis] feet. I expected my [combatant_2.GetRootRelation] to land a blow or two, but I did not expect the [From.GetManWoman] to want to join us even more afterwards.
Just as [combatant_2.GetTitledName] was about to show [From.GetTitledName] what a sparring match looks like, the [From.GetAgeAdjective] [From.GetManWoman] dropped [From.GetHerHis] weapon and ran.
Now that is what we want to see!
Another member? Good.
Still standing? Then welcome.
What a waste of a morning!
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be invited to join §Y[Root.Society.GetName]§!.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! will be §Rbanned§! from joining §Y[Root.Society.GetName]§! for 10 years.

To [Root.GetTitledName],

Not a drop of your own blood was spilled, and that is a rare thing. The Gods have seen it. Come and take your place among [From.Society.GetName], and know that from now on every battle is an offering, and every offering is watched.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You bled, and you did not kneel. Good. Blood is the first coin of the Gods, and you have paid it. Your place among [From.Society.GetName] is waiting. Bring your scars. There will be more.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

Not one scratch! Very good, very cunning. Too cunning, maybe? I will watch you, yes-yes. Come, you are of [From.Society.GetName] now. Serve well. Serve ME well, most of all.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You bleed-bled but you did not run-flee. Strange-brave! Come, you are of [From.Society.GetName] now. Lick the wounds and sharpen the claws. There is much killing to do, yes-yes.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Dat woz a proper krumpin'! Not even a scratch on ya. Da boyz are well impressed (an' a bit narked). Ya'z one of [From.Society.GetName] now. Get in 'ere an' find a choppa.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Ya got bashed up good, but ya kept standin'. Dat's da Orky way. Ya'z one of [From.Society.GetName] now. Da scars make ya look 'arder anyway.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledName],

The yard saw no blood of yours today, and the old warriors are still talking about it. The Wolf favours the strong, and you have shown your strength. Come to the fire. Your place among [From.Society.GetName] is waiting.

In Ulric's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You took your wounds like a warrior and you stood up again. Ulric asks no more than that. Come to the fire, and let the brothers and sisters of [From.Society.GetName] drink to your scars.

In Ulric's name,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the valiant [Root.GetTitledName],

I am told you came through the passage of arms without a single scratch. That is the kind of [Root.GetWarriorRole] this order would be honoured to count among its own. You are hereby invited to take your vows with [From.Society.GetName].

With respect,
[From.GetTitledName]

To the brave [Root.GetTitledName],

You were wounded in the passage of arms, yet you held to the end and yielded to no one. Courage under pain is the first virtue of a knight. You are hereby invited to take your vows with [From.Society.GetName].

With respect,
[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

The elders watched, and the elders were satisfied, which is not a thing I write often. Not a scratch on you. Your name is entered among [From.Society.GetName]. Do not make us strike it out.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledName],

You were hurt and you did not yield. A dwarf does not yield. The elders have entered your name among [From.Society.GetName]. Get those wounds seen to, and then get back to the drill yard.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the valiant [Root.GetTitledName],

I am told you did not take a single scratch during your initiation! That is the kind of [Root.GetWarriorRole] we would be honoured to have at our table. You are hereby invited to join our ranks.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the brave [Root.GetTitledName],

You were hurt during your initiation, but you stayed on your feet, and that is what we ask. You are hereby invited to join our ranks.

[From.GetTitledName]
Glory to the Gods.
Yes-yes! I am of the Warlords!
WAAAGH!
Ulric hears.
I shall take my vows with pride.
About time.
Finally.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! also sends you a white wolf pelt from the lodge's own trophies.

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You ran. The Gods saw it, and they laughed. Do not come to us again. If you do, you will be the offering.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You flee-fled! Even a slave-rat fights when cornered. Go away-away. Come back and I will have you skinned, yes-yes.

[From.GetTitledName], Warlord

Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]!

Ya ran off like a grot wiv a squig on 'is bum. Da boyz ain't stopped laughin'. Don't come back or we'z gonna krump ya proper.

[From.GetFirstName], da Boss

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

A wolf does not run from a fight. You did. Do not seek our fire again for many winters, or you will find it colder than you think.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You abandoned the passage of arms before witnesses. There is no place in [From.Society.GetName] for those who flee the field. Do not seek our gates for many years to come.

[From.GetTitledName]

To [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

You ran. It has been written down. Do not come back to the Guild until a long time has passed, and even then, expect the elders to remember.

[From.GetTitledName]

To the COWARD [Root.GetTitledFirstName],

Needless to say, we are unimpressed by your behaviour, and hope you do not seek us out again any time soon, lest this offence escalate.

[From.GetTitledName]
The Gods can laugh all they like.
Not-fair! Not-fair!
Dey'll be sorry!
I am as ashamed as you are.
I have dishonoured myself.
I'll not forget this either.
I am as disappointed as you are.
You will be unable to join §Y[martial_society_to_join.GetName]§! for 10 years.

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is in a strange mood at dinner tonight, talking about the Gods and how they look on those who only watch. Then [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] sets down the knife. "Enough, [Root.GetFirstName]. When will you take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]? I did not raise you to grow old and forgotten."

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] watches me eat with narrow eyes. "You are big-strong now, yes? Strong enough to fight for the Warlords? [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName] needs claws. Mine are many. Yours... we will see-see, yes? Unless you are afraid-scared."

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] bangs da table so 'ard da grub jumps. "Oi, [Root.GetFirstName]! Ya'z big enuff now. When ya gonna join [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName] an' do some proper fightin'? I ain't 'avin' no runt in da family!"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] keeps glancing at my sword arm over dinner, and talking about the winter hunts of [recruiting_parent.GetHerHis] youth. At last [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] says it plainly. "The Wolf is calling you, [Root.GetFirstName]. When will you stand in the yard and take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is making some less than subtle remarks over dinner, about my horsemanship and my skill at arms. "Honestly, [Root.GetFirstName]," [recruiting_parent.GetSheHe] says at last, "when are you going to seek your spurs with [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] puts down [recruiting_parent.GetHerHis] tankard and looks at me across the table. "My own father was in the Guild. I am in the Guild. When are you going to stop hiding behind your beard and take the trial of [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"

My [recruiting_parent.GetRootRelation] is making some less than subtle remarks over dinner, about my swordsmanship and how interested I am in war. "Honestly, [Root.GetFirstName]... when are you going to join [recruiting_parent.Society.GetName]?"
I have only been waiting for you to ask.
§Y[champion_character.GetTitledFirstName]§! of [martial_society_to_join.GetName] will be told.
[recruiting_parent.GetFatherMotherCap], I will carve my own path.
Your [recruiting_parent.GetFatherMother] will be disappointed.
My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] breaks into a broad grin. "I thought you would never ask! I will go to [champion_character.GetTitledFirstName] at once, [Root.GetFatherMother]."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] breaks into a broad grin. "I thought you would never ask!" Then the grin fades a little. "Wait. You are the one I have to face, aren't you? You will go easy on me, [Root.GetFatherMother]?"

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] rolls [new_recruit.GetHerHis] eyes. "I will carve my own path, [Root.GetFatherMother]. Please, let me." When I say nothing, [new_recruit.GetSheHe] goes on: "And [champion_character.GetSocietyRank] [champion_character.GetTitledFirstName] is a bore."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] rolls [new_recruit.GetHerHis] eyes. "I will carve my own path, [Root.GetFatherMother]. And I am not going to fight in a yard so you can judge me in front of your friends."
I was only waiting for you to be ready!
We'll do this properly. You're a recruit like any other!
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will tell you how the trial went.
Why, you ungrateful little...!
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! is clearly not ready for this.

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and cannot stop talking about the initiation duel. "It was wonderful, [Root.GetFatherMother]! And now I am one of [new_recruit.Society.GetName]!"
I knew you had it in you, [new_recruit.GetFirstName].
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! has joined §Y[new_recruit.Society.GetName]§!.
You almost make me wish I had never left...
You feel a little homesick for the old days.
Are you trying to impress me or something?
You scowl at the excited [new_recruit.GetManWoman].

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and says nothing for what feels like an eternity. When I try to coax a word out of the [new_recruit.GetBoyGirl], [new_recruit.GetSheHe] mumbles, red with shame: "I am not like you, [Root.GetFatherMother]. I failed the trial."

My [new_recruit.GetSonDaughter] comes to dinner tonight and says nothing for what feels like an eternity. When I try to coax a word out of the [new_recruit.GetBoyGirl], [new_recruit.GetSheHe] mumbles: "Don't be angry. I changed my mind about joining [Root.Society.GetName]."
Oh dear... I am still proud to call you family, [new_recruit.GetFirstName].
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! will get over it.
I expected more, honestly.
§Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! blinks away a tear.
Weakness has no place in my blood.
You kill §Y[new_recruit.GetTitledFirstName]§! where [new_recruit.GetSheHe] sits.

My [From.GetFatherMother] tells me it does not matter which road I walk. "Sword or quill, you are my [Root.GetSonDaughter]." We spend the rest of the evening talking about other hopes and dreams of mine, and I smile whenever I think of it.
My [From.GetFatherMother] tells me [From.GetSheHe] expected more from me, then finishes [From.GetHerHis] dinner in silence.\n\nI feel awful.
Family is what matters most, after all.
I am lucky to have [From.GetHerHim].
This is not the end of my story! Nay, [From.GetSheHe] doesn't KNOW me...!
You'll show [From.GetHerHim]...!
I am an embarrassment.
My [Root.GetDuelWeapon] moves as easily as breathing now. I have learned what single combat can teach me, and perhaps it is time I turned to the other arts that [Root.Society.GetName] prizes.
I have read every campaign worth reading and fought a few worth writing about. Perhaps it is time I turned to something else.
There is no beast in these forests whose track I cannot read, and the hunt has lost its edge. Perhaps it is time I turned to something else.
I should focus on single combat.
I want to go deeper into the art of war.
I want to return to the hunt.
On second thought, I like my life as it is.

The old warriors of [Root.Society.GetName] have long wondered which road I will take. Some live for the duel in the snow, some for the war council, and some, like Ulric's own wolves, for the long hunt through the winter forests.

My brothers and sisters of [Root.Society.GetName] have long been asking when I will choose my calling. Some seek glory in the joust and the duel, others in the command of armies, and others still in the hunt, as the knights of the forest marches did in the old days.

The elders of [Root.Society.GetName] have been asking which craft of war I mean to master. Some dwarfs are known for their axe-work, some for holding a line that never breaks, and some for hunting goblins through the deeps until not one is left.
My fellow members of [Root.Society.GetName] have long been wondering when I will choose a focus for my fighting talents. Some live for the duel, others for the art of war, and others for the hunt.
I should focus on single combat.
This will lead to the §YDuelist§! trait.
I want to go deeper into the art of war.
This will lead to the §YStrategist§! trait.
I will learn the ways of the hunt.
This will lead to the §YHunter§! trait.

I have watched my warriors at their practice in the yard, and I am sure some of them grow uneasy under the constant eye of their [Root.GetTitle]. Perhaps I should admit that my own swordplay could use some guidance. If nothing else, I could join them in the snow.
I have watched the squires at their drill, and next to theirs my own blade work has grown rusty. A knight is judged in the lists. Perhaps it is time I took up the sword in earnest.
I have watched the young dwarfs at their axe-drill, and I know my own work is not what it should be. An axe that is not used grows dull, and so does the arm that swings it.

I have watched my soldiers practise their swordsmanship, and I am sure some of them are unsettled by the constant watch of their [Root.GetTitle]. Perhaps I should admit that I could use some guidance with my own blade. If nothing else, I could join their training.
I shall ask [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] to teach me all [mentor_target.GetSheHe] knows.
I will quietly hire a master of the blade.
I would rather do this alone.

My [From.GetRootRelation] [From.GetTitledFirstName] of [From.Society.GetName] has sent word asking for private lessons in single combat. "The [From.GetTitle] would value any guidance you can offer, my [Root.GetLordLady]," the messenger says.
I will set up [From.GetHerHis] training myself.
I will lend [From.GetHerHim] some of my best veterans to spar with.

When we started practising together, I could hardly imagine having the kind of confidence that [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] shows on the battlefield. But with [mentor_target.GetHerHis] training behind me, I think I have truly found my calling.

The last time we spoke, [mentor_target.GetTitledFirstName] had only praise for me. It is an odd feeling that [mentor_target.GetSheHe] is not here to see me now. I let out a sigh and clear my mind, feeling the [Root.GetDuelWeapon] in my hand. It is so natural to me now, as if part of my body.

Careful where you point that thing! a courtier cries out as I stroll back from yet another session at the training grounds, idly spinning my blade. Then, hurriedly: "Of course, a master duelist such as yourself knows best, my [Root.GetLordLady]."
I will always be grateful for your lessons, [mentor_target.GetFirstName].
A master, am I? Why, yes, I suppose I am!
It took time, but all that hard work has paid off!

My scholars have stacked old campaign books in front of me: Magnus at the gates of Kislev, the Wolf-Kings of Middenheim, the winter wars against the north. Should I not be out with the warriors instead, learning on the field?

The order's library holds the great treatises of war: the campaigns of Magnus the Pious, the Myrmidian manuals of Tilea, the old chronicles of the Emperor's wars. My scholars say every commander begins here. But surely I belong on the field, not at a desk?

The lore-keepers have brought out the Book of Battles of my hold, every engagement since the Time of Woes written down to the last cart of ale. Reading it would take years. Then again, I could simply go and watch the hold's warriors drill.

The stack of books in front of me is daunting. My scholars say these are the classics for anyone who would understand war. But surely I do not need the basics? Should I not be out in the field, watching the troops first-hand?
There is wisdom in the old campaigns.
I learn better by watching.

My commanders have come to ask my advice on the exercises they are running outside the walls of my [Root.GetCapitalHolding]. "We could use that strategic mind of yours, [Root.GetMasterMistress]," they say. Startled, I realise that my studies have paid off, and my chest swells with pride. Then I collect myself and nod: "Of course. I'd be glad to help."
Typically, what you'll want to consider in a set-up like this...
Soon you are talking and gesturing with enthusiasm, to an even mix of "Oohs" and "Aaahs".

The huntmasters of [Root.Society.GetName] say a warrior of the Wolf must follow a trail through snow and forest as the wolf does. They have offered to take me out into the Drakwald. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set snares?
The order's huntsmen have agreed to teach me, as the knights of old learned to hunt boar and beastmen in the great forests. Should I learn to follow a trail, or to lay traps?

The rangers of [Root.Society.GetName] know every tunnel and every gully, and how to hunt goblins and worse through all of them. They have offered to take me along. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set traps?
The huntsmen I have been riding with are pleased with my progress and ask what I would like to learn next. Should I learn to read tracks, or to set traps?
Tracking. I want to read the forest like a book.
Traps. Let the prey come to me.

We have been tracking for hours through the snow when I hear a sound in the brush. A thunk, a soft groan, and I know my arrow has found its mark. "Ulric's own wolves could not have done better!" one of my companions laughs. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!"

The hounds have lost the scent, but I have not. I lead the hunting party to the thicket, and there the great boar stands. One spear, well placed, and it is over. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!" one of my companions laughs. I smile.

Three days in the deeps, and the goblin raiders thought they had lost us. They had not. When the last of them falls, a ranger claps me on the shoulder. "You hunt like one of the old ones, [Root.GetFirstName]. They should call you the Hunter."

We have been tracking for hours when I hear a sound in the bushes. A thunk, followed by a soft groan, tells me that my arrow has found its mark. "They should call you [Root.GetFirstName] the Hunter!" one of my companions laughs. I smile.
I can't believe I wasn't always like this.

Ulric would be proud of you, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me as we stand in the snow, our breath steaming. "You have the wolf in you now. When the enemy sees you coming, they will remember the winters."

Khaine himself would smile at you, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] says, wiping [fellow_member.GetHerHis] blade on a slave's tunic. "You have learned the corsair's art. Now choose what you want most from the coasts of the lesser races: their gold, their blood, or their bodies in chains."

You've the makings of a proper captain, [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me over a cup of rum. "But a crew needs to know what its captain is after. Is it the plunder, the fight, or the slave markets of Sartosa?"
The dedication you show is admirable, [Root.GetSisterBrother], [fellow_member.GetTitledFirstName] tells me. "You have learned all we can teach."
Thank you, [fellow_member.GetFirstName]. That means a lot.
In your heart, you feel that [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] might frown upon your devotion to these people.
The plunder. Always the plunder.
The raid. Fire and steel from the sea.
Slaves. They fetch the best price.
Da old cut 'as closed up, leavin' a nice big scar. Orks don't stay 'urt. A bit o' fresh air an' a good scrap or two round [Root.Location.GetName] woz all I needed!
Da shaman said I woz done for. Da shaman woz wrong. Me guts 'ave knitted up by demselves, like dey always do. Maybe I'll krump da shaman for lyin'.
Da stump's 'ealed up proper, an' I'z used to it now. Da boyz say it makes me look 'arder. Dey'z right.
I woz smashed up so bad da boyz woz arguin' over who gets me teef. Den I woke up dis mornin', got up, an' stood up straight. "Dat's da Orky way," I tell da grot starin' at me. "Now get me some grub."
Da wound woz goin' green, an' not da good kind o' green. A painboy slapped some squig paste on it, an' now da stink's gone. Just a scar left. Lovely.
Feelin' 'arder already!
Gork's wiv me! Dat's why I don't die!
Mork's wiv me! 'E's too kunnin' ta let me croak!

Someone get me an axe! I roar. The crowd gasps as I start swinging it about, some scrambling in panic to get out of my way. One brave soul, [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName], steps up to meet me. When we are done we are both laughing. "I like your rage, [Root.GetBrotherSister]!" [kinslayer_target.GetSheHe] says, wiping the sweat from [kinslayer_target.GetHerHis] brow.

Someone get me an axe! NOW! I roar at the nearest soldier. From the corner of my eye I see my [kinslayer_target.GetRootRelation] [kinslayer_target.GetTitledFirstName] watching me. As I start swinging, the rush of battle fills me, and I find myself laughing from the bottom of my belly. [kinslayer_target.GetFirstName] is laughing too, and the crowd cheers me on.
